text:
**Change:** Cc goes from 1.0 pF to 0.8 pF. Nothing else changes.

**Why:** UGBW is the only failing spec, at 22.1 MHz against a 25 MHz target. UGBW scales roughly as gm1/Cc. With the n1 parasitic capacitance included, 0.8 pF should land it near 27 MHz. PM was 86.6°, so there is plenty of margin to give up some phase. The second-stage gm is unchanged, so the non-dominant pole stays put. Rz = 10 kΩ still places the zero well out. This is an estimate and has not been simulated; I expect PM to stay above 70°.

The other specs should not move meaningfully. Power and bias currents are unchanged. Gain, noise, CMRR, PSRR and swing do not depend on Cc. Slew rate improves, to roughly 10 µA / 0.8 pF ≈ 12 V/µs.

```spice
.subckt dut vinp vinn vout vdd vss ibias
* bias: reference diode sinks IREF
MB0 ibias ibias vss vss nfet W=1.25 L=0.5 m=8
* tail current source (10 uA)
MB1 tail ibias vss vss nfet W=1.25 L=0.5 m=8
* NMOS input pair (vinp on output side -> non-inverting)
M1 d1 vinn tail vss nfet W=5 L=2 m=10
M2 n1 vinp tail vss nfet W=5 L=2 m=10
* PMOS mirror load
M3 d1 d1 vdd vdd pfet W=2.4 L=0.6 m=2
M4 n1 d1 vdd vdd pfet W=2.4 L=0.6 m=2
* second stage: PMOS pull-up (~16 uA)
M7 vout n1 vdd vdd pfet W=2.2 L=0.6 m=7
* second stage: NMOS pull-down, DC-biased from mirror, AC-driven from n1
M8 vout g8 vss vss nfet W=1.25 L=0.5 m=13
Cb n1 g8 1p
Rb g8 ibias 20e6
* Miller compensation with nulling resistor (Cc reduced to raise UGBW)
Rz n1 nc 10k
Cc nc vout 0.8p
.ends
```
